note: Adapted from the species-level description in Sands (1972), originally in English; the alate is based only on old specimens, whose colour the original states to have faded in preservation. The genus has no soldiers, hence the absence of a soldier section; synonymy, measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: All necessary comparisons have been made in the discussions of the remaining species. The discussion of the genus shows that the worker enteric valve armature forms a series; apart from an unnamed species known only from workers, the present species represents the most primitive condition in that series. The species is known only from the type series.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, pilosity sparse and yellow. Postclypeus weakly convex, Pcl/W 0.25. Apical tooth of mandibles short, L/L1 0.63, Ra/Ri 0.82; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible, in surface view, separated from the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 10.41; apex of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible slightly posterior to the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margins of the two marginal teeth about equal in length, Ra/Rj·Rm 11.00. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.73, third apical spur vestigial and very minute. Mesenteron–proctodaeum junction oblique; valve seat connected by a distinct neck to the second proctodaeal pouch, situated dorsolaterally in the undissected abdomen; the valve cushion in position 1 sclerotized only in its distal half, the part projecting beyond the tips of the spines of the other cushions comprising only about one quarter of its total length, the swollen distal margin bearing 13–18 slender spines, the remaining length (including the unsclerotized base) with small spines; margins of the remaining cushions bearing 5–10 slender curved spines that taper abruptly to almost blunt tips, the rest of the cushions with small spines; valve membrane with distinguishable minute spines between and outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule sepia brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle short oval, flat or slightly concave, sometimes almost as large as an ocellus, slightly paler than the head capsule; median spot short oval, much smaller than the fontanelle, flat or slightly raised, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus sepia brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark nearly flat, shining and crescent-shaped, slightly paler than the head capsule; antennae pale brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum sepia brown, transverse dark sutures distinct; femora brown, tibiae and tarsi pale brown. Abdominal tergites sepia brown, sternites brown and paler medially, dorsal and ventral spiracles darker than the sclerites; cerci very pale brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule evenly rounded, ocelli small, separated from the compound eye by nearly one and a half times their minimum diameter; postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.29, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct except in the anterior third. Apical tooth of mandibles short, L/L1 0.51, Ra/Ri 0.66; accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible, in surface view, separated from the molar prominence, La/Li·Lm 5.33; apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible with their apices in a line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth longer than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum of moderate width at the constriction, M/W 0.30. Pilosity of the head capsule forming a slightly uneven fur, with protruding setae. Third apical spur of the fore tibia vestigial.
